A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PartDiffuser. All 12 pages of v1 and 13 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison. Relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original mesh-generation experiments on Objaverse, HSSD and 3DFront, conditioning ablations, and an appendix sampling-efficiency study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds quantitative and qualitative evaluation using an alternative upstream segmenter.

M1.justification: The representation, part-wise autoregression, discrete diffusion, hierarchical conditioning, loss and sampling pseudocode are retained. The feed-forward block clarified in v2 was already depicted in v1 Figure 2. Added curriculum and sampler descriptions do not establish a newly introduced algorithm.

E1.justification: Training still uses Objaverse and 3DFront, and evaluation covers Objaverse, HSSD and 3DFront point-cloud-to-mesh generation. The SAMPart3D experiment varies segmentation preprocessing within existing Objaverse coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains MeshAnythingV2, BPT and TreeMeshGPT. Appendix C.1 adds an evaluated upstream-method comparison: PartDiffuser using SAMPart3D segmentation versus its original PartField segmentation. SAMPart3D is not presented as an independent mesh-generation baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 revises the reported training budget from two weeks on four H100 GPUs to three days on eight H100s followed by two weeks on four. v2 also adds the segmenter-substitution evaluation. Existing splits, metrics and acceleration settings remain unchanged; benchmark reruns are not established.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 adds segmentation robustness analysis using SAMPart3D, with Chamfer Distance and two visual examples. Existing conditioning ablations and sampling-efficiency sensitivity results remain; the efficiency study moves from v1 Appendix B.2 to v2 Section 4.5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new robustness result introduces no statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical scores and timings in Tables 1–3 are unchanged. v2 newly reports Objaverse CD of 19.11 × 10^-3 with SAMPart3D, alongside the retained PartField score rounded to 17.81 × 10^-3, and adds Figure 8's qualitative comparison. These are results under alternative segmentation, not a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: The likelihood factorization, diffusion objective and segmentation-bound formulas are retained, with no new proofs or formal assumptions. Renaming the cross-attention output and explaining the already depicted feed-forward block clarify the architecture without adding substantive mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about semi-autoregressive mesh generation, hierarchical conditioning, global coherence and local fidelity. The new robustness evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new segmentation experiment as evidence of robustness and explains how coarse partitions can exhaust token capacity and simplify detail. It adds a lower-confidence-token explanation for acceleration artifacts and softens the sampling visualization's connectivity inference from confirmation to a possible explanation.

D1.justification: v2 documents clipped-noise pretraining followed by full-range fine-tuning, expands hardware/time accounting, and explicitly identifies LLaDA sampling. However, it removes v1's cosine learning-rate schedule from 3 × 10^-4 to 1 × 10^-5 and leaves the new clipping bounds unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds BANG to the part-level generation discussion and cites SAMPart3D for the robustness experiment. The broader positioning relative to autoregressive mesh generators and block diffusion remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Targeted restructuring shortens the main training/sampling explanation, collects details in Appendix B, and moves efficiency analysis into Section 4.5. Most prose remains unchanged. v2 also adds acknowledgments and changes the corresponding-author marker.

P2.justification: v2 adds robustness Figure 8, refines Figure 2's conditioning labels/arrows, and updates the parts-only ablation rendering. It relocates the gallery, attention-mask illustration, sampling algorithm and efficiency displays, and clarifies table/figure labels. Existing visual designs and numerical table contents are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v2 partially addresses the previously untested sensitivity to upstream segmentation with quantitative and visual evidence, while clarifying training stages and the block description. These modest gains outweigh the limited documentation losses, although removal of the learning-rate schedule and unspecified clipping bounds constrain reproducibility. The principal benchmark evidence remains unchanged.
